messages:
alice.z: Heads-up — after the eu-west controlplane cutover some tenants observed requests routed to the old region for ~3m. Seems like split-horizon DNS + regional AnycastLB rules interacting badly.
bob.l: any packet traces or DNS answers?
alice.z: grabbed resolver logs: region-local resolvers returned A records for cp.eu-west.redwood.internal that pointed to the old AZ IP for a subset of queries. The controlplane updated records immediately but the regional DNS caches and LB edge had stale mappings.
chris.m: did clients have cached TTLs? or was this resolver-side?
alice.z: TL;DR: short TTLs on public records but our internal split-horizon name got faster failover because of per-node hostfile overrides in the old rollout automation. The hostfile entries caused some nodes to bypass DNS and keep hitting old IPs.
sophia.p: hostfile overrides? where are those coming from?
alice.z: rollout script for region pinning wrote /etc/hosts entries during canary to force local testing. Forgot to remove for some tenants in the push.
bob.l: ouch. That explains why DNS invalidation didn't help. We need a safer rollout pattern.
chris.m: options: 1) remove hostfile usage entirely and rely on DNS with active invalidation; 2) make hostfile entries ephemeral and tied to process lifecycle; 3) add rollout hooks to atomically flip both hostfile and DNS and emit a verification probe.
sophia.p: we should also harden the LB routing to prefer controlplane-signed route epochs rather than relying purely on name resolution. If relay routing honors epoch metadata, it can avoid depending on DNS correctness for short windows.
alice.z: agree. Short-term fix: remove the hostfile writes from the rollout scripts and run a forced cache flush on affected nodes. Also add a post-rollout probe that resolves cp hostnames and hits a synthetic health endpoint to verify region identity.
bob.l: long-term: propose RFC "split-horizon-safety-and-rollout-atomicity" — include: ban hostfile usage in automation, add route-epoching at relay for authoritative handoff, and a cache-invalidation webhook for internal resolvers.
chris.m: for the cache-invalidation webhook, naive fanout to region resolvers is fine. We'll add exponential backoff and a metric invalidation_failures.
sophia.p: add guardrails in CI: disallow any change that writes to /etc/hosts in deploy scripts unless explicitly reviewed and flagged.
alice.z: Plan: (1) revert hostfile writes in next canary (2) run resolver flush + synthetic probe for currently impacted tenants (3) implement probe + webhook in 2 weeks as quick followups (4) open RFC.
infra-bot: revert rollout: region-pin-canary -> staging queued at 2025-07-22T09:00:00Z
bob.l: tagging SRE: @chris.m can you run the synthetic probes and collect stale_hostfile_count metric?
chris.m: on it. I'll post results in here after probes run.
alice.z: thanks everyone. Follow-up RFC will be brief; I'll open after probe results.
